payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-07-01
payload.summary:
**Claude Sonnet 5** flips to default across the stack, while Linux desktop support finally lands; **Fable** rumors hijack the timeline, with builders literally waiting up for midnight; **Vercel Services** and a new **Shopify** linkup sharpen the agentic web story; Dylan Patel's big point cuts through the noise: **AI's real 100x may come from hardware-software co-design, not model theatrics alone**.

**Sonnet 5** 直接铺到全线，Linux 版桌面端也补上了；**Fable** 把整条时间线搅热，一群人真在等午夜刷新；**Vercel Services** 加上和 **Shopify** 的联动，把 agentic web 这条线又拧紧了一圈；Dylan Patel 这期最扎实的一句是：**AI 真正的 100 倍，不一定在模型口号里，更可能在硬件和软件一起重做这件事上**。

sections.headline: **Hardware-software co-design** is AI's real 100x / **硬软协同**才是 AI 真正的 100 倍杠杆
sections.body:
In this **Training Data** episode, Dylan Patel argues that the next real leap in AI comes from rebuilding the full stack together: chips, systems, costs, and software behavior. He keeps coming back to the same point: model gains alone are not enough if inference still rides on hardware that was never built for the way LLMs run.

The backstory is half obsession, half accident. Patel traces **SemiAnalysis** from fixing an **Xbox 360** with the red ring of death, to years deep in hardware forums, to a COVID-era break that turned anonymous posting into a real research business. The throughline is unusually consistent: follow the technical details, but never stop asking what they cost and who can scale them.

这期 **Training Data** 里，Dylan Patel 讲得很直接：AI 下一次真正拉开差距，不是模型单点猛冲，而是把芯片、系统、成本和软件行为一起重做。他反复盯住一个问题不放：如果推理还跑在并不是为 LLM 设计的硬件上，单靠模型涨分，天花板很快就会撞上。

他的来路也挺野。先是为修一台红环的 **Xbox 360** 扎进硬件世界，后来长期泡论坛、盯供应链、看架构；再到疫情那阵子，把匿名发帖硬生生写成了 **SemiAnalysis**。主线一直没变：技术细节要看，成本更得看，最后是谁真能把它规模化。

sections.headline: Traditional PM habits choke AI-native imagination / 传统 PM 习惯卡住 AI 原生想象力
sections.body:
The biggest challenge for trad PMs trying to adapt to AI native building is a lack of magical thinking. A decade of frameworks, “agile” and metric obsession has led to constraint-first, incremental thinking.

I used to combat this on my teams by asking them to  imagine we had tech from 100 yrs in the future, the experiences it would enable and working backward from that. the ideas would always be far more creative.

the funny thing is, that technology from the future is here.

go build that magical thing!

传统 PM 想转到 AI native 的最大问题，是缺少那种“先把魔法想出来”的劲头。十年下来，各种框架、“agile”和指标崇拜，把人训练成先看限制、只敢做小修小补。

我以前带团队时，会故意反着来：先假设我们手里有一百年后的技术，想清楚它能做出什么体验，再倒推回来。这样出来的点子，通常都更有创造力。

好笑的是，那种“未来技术”现在已经在这了。

去把那个像魔法的东西做出来吧！

sections.headline: Frontier releases may now come with a government-tested playbook / 前沿模型发布可能开始走政府协同剧本
sections.body:
Things seem to be ending up in a better spot with Fable, and presumably GPT-5.6 next. What we have now is the initial precedent for what frontier model releases (or at least those that have significant coding and cyber capabilities) could look like going forward. This would presumably apply to bio and other categories of risk that have been identified by AI safety groups. 

From the Anthropic post:

“3. A shared industry framework. Although we have reached a constructive resolution, these events have made clear that the industry needs a consistent way to assess and fix potential “jailbreaks” of AI models (techniques that bypass a model’s safeguards).2 A shared standard for judging the severity of a given jailbreak would help AI developers triage new findings as they arise, launch highly-capable models with greater safety, and communicate the level of risk consistently to government and industry partners. Together with Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and other Glasswing partners, we’ve started to develop such a framework, and we outline it below.

4. Deeper government collaboration. We’re also strengthening our level of collaboration with the US government on new pre-release testing, information sharing, and research collaboration. We describe this deeper collaboration in the final section.”

It’s been a messy process to get here, but at least there’s some semblance of a framework that could be practical. The only note of caution here would be that there’s a lot of subjectivity that goes into various risks and their actual levels of exploitability in practice. We’re likely going to be living with a framework that requires heavy judgment and back and forth between labs and the government for major releases.

The best we can hope for is that this is a relatively efficient process, and hopefully has ways of being sped up for incremental version updates in models. It would be a bad outcome if every release after this level of threshold of capability required the same review process, and we don’t get the same rate of breakthroughs we’ve been seeing.

看起来 Fable 这件事最后落在了一个相对更好的位置上，接下来大概 GPT-5.6 也会照着走。现在摆在眼前的，是一个初步先例：以后前沿模型发布，尤其是那些在编码和网络安全能力上很强的模型，可能就会按这种方式推进。按这个逻辑，生物等其他已被 AI 安全团队点名的风险类别，估计也会套进来。

Anthropic 文里写道：

“3. 一个共享的行业框架。虽然我们已经达成了一个建设性的解决方案，但这些事件已经清楚说明，行业需要一种一致的方法来评估和修复 AI 模型潜在的‘越狱’（也就是绕过模型防护的技术）。一个共享的严重性判断标准，可以帮助 AI 开发者在新发现出现时做分级处理，更安全地发布高能力模型，也能让他们向政府和行业伙伴更一致地传达风险水平。我们已经和 Amazon、Microsoft、Google 以及其他 Glasswing 合作伙伴开始制定这样的框架，下面也会做说明。

4. 更深入的政府协作。我们也在加强和美国政府之间的新一轮发布前测试、信息共享和研究合作。最后一节会介绍这部分内容。”

走到这一步过程很乱，但至少现在像是有了个还能落地的框架。需要留神的是，很多风险判断以及它们在现实里到底多容易被利用，本来就带着很强的主观性。接下来大模型重大发布，多半都会卡在实验室和政府来回拉扯、反复判断里。

最好的情况，是这个流程别太慢，而且模型做小版本更新时还能走得快一点。要是今后只要能力一过线，每次发布都得重走一遍同样的审查，那推进速度肯定要掉下来。

sections.headline: **Box** says **Sonnet 5** beats **Sonnet 4.6** on enterprise document work / **Box** 称 **Sonnet 5** 在企业文档任务上超过 **Sonnet 4.6**
sections.body:
We've been running Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5 through the Box AI Complex Work Eval, our agentic benchmark that puts models through real enterprise document work end-to-end.

Sonnet 5 holds frontier-class quality on complex multi-step work and pulls ahead of Sonnet 4.6 in several core enterprise domains like Energy (+4.7pp), Retail (+4.4pp), and Professional Services (+2.6pp), and other spaces where unstructured data is heavily complex.

Here are a few examples of wins compared to Sonnet 4.6 to get a sense of some of the more advanced reasoning capabilities in Sonnet 5:

* Financing due diligence: It computed the company's liquidity and leverage ratios from the raw balance sheet, and caught that the source report's own stated debt-to-equity figure understated the leverage, flagging all three loan covenants as violated, not just the ones the document admitted.

* Overhaul cost analysis: It scoped "total cost" to the company's own KPI definitions, correctly separating out Lost Production Cost because the guidance said to track it separately rather than naively summing every number on the sheet. It also caught and handled a broken reference cell in the spreadsheet.

* SKU revenue analysis: On segmented sales data, it computed each product's contribution against the correct subcategory denominator, sidestepping the easy mistake of dividing by the category total, and flagged why no Pet-category SKU cracked the top 9.

Sonnet 5 will be available in the Box AI Studio shortly for customers to build custom agents with.

我们一直在用 Anthropic 的 Claude Sonnet 5 跑 Box AI Complex Work Eval，这是我们的 agentic 基准，用真实的企业文档任务把模型从头到尾过一遍。

Sonnet 5 在复杂多步骤任务上维持住了前沿水准，而且在几个核心企业领域超过了 Sonnet 4.6，比如能源（+4.7 个百分点）、零售（+4.4 个百分点）和专业服务（+2.6 个百分点），尤其是在那些非结构化数据又多又乱的场景里。

下面是几个相对 Sonnet 4.6 更能说明 Sonnet 5 推理能力的例子：

* 融资尽调：它能直接从原始资产负债表算出公司的流动性和杠杆比率，还发现源报告自己写的 debt-to-equity 数字把杠杆写低了，因此判定三项贷款契约全部违约，而不是只指出文件里承认的那几项。

* 大修成本分析：它会按公司自己的 KPI 定义去界定“total cost”，把 Lost Production Cost 正确拆出去，因为指导里明确说这项要单独跟踪，而不是把表上所有数字一股脑相加。它还识别并处理了电子表格里一个坏掉的引用单元格。

* SKU 收入分析：在分段销售数据里，它按正确的子品类分母去计算每个产品的贡献占比，避开了直接拿品类总额去除这种常见错误，也指出了为什么没有任何宠物类 SKU 进入前 9。

Sonnet 5 很快会进 Box AI Studio，客户可以直接拿它来搭自定义 agent。

sections.headline: More AI adoption, more hiring? / AI 用得越多，反而越招人？
sections.body:
More data is showing the opposite of what many people expected with AI adoption and jobs. Ramp found that the more AI adoption a company has the more their headcount grows.

At Box, we recently did a survey of 1,600+ mid and large sized companies, and the findings were similar. 58% of respondents expected headcount to rise over the next three years. Interestingly, that figure climbs to 79% among the most mature adopters of AI. The more advanced AI adopters expected to grow their headcount at a greater rate in the future than others.

Of course it's true that the companies that can afford to adopt AI the most are also the ones that likely are seeing growth in their business, leading to more headcount. So the point of the story isn't necessarily that by adopting AI you will inherently grow. 

*But* the most important takeaway is that the opposite is not proving out. The fears a couple years ago would have been that the companies adopting AI the most would be hiring fewer people. 

But in reality this is what actually you should expect to happen. If a company can get more customers because they use AI in sales for account or market intelligence, they hire more sales people not fewer. If you can build way more software than before, you end up hiring more engineers because the projects get bigger and you take on more. And so on.

越来越多的数据，正在给“AI 上来就会砍岗位”这个预期泼冷水。Ramp 发现，一家公司 AI 用得越深，员工规模反而越会增长。

Box 最近也调查了 1600 多家中大型公司，结果差不多。58% 的受访者预计未来三年 headcount 会增加；而在最成熟的 AI 采用者里，这个数字升到 79%。也就是说，AI 用得更深的公司，反而更预期自己以后会招更多人。

当然也得承认，那些最有条件上 AI 的公司，本来往往业务就在增长，所以 headcount 才会上去。这个结论不是说“用了 AI 就一定会长”。

但关键点在于，至少反过来的故事并没有被数据撑住。前几年大家担心的是，最积极用 AI 的公司会最先少招人。

现实看起来更像另一套逻辑：如果 AI 帮你拿到更多客户，比如销售靠它做客户和市场情报，你通常会招更多销售，不是更少；如果你能比以前做出更多软件，项目盘子会变大，工程师也常常会继续加。
